title: Abbasid Samarra: Pipeline Validation Sample

evidence.title_angle: What Samarra preserves of the Abbasid world
evidence.thumbnail_visual_story: A surviving spiral minaret rises above unoccupied brick ruins on the right in warm daylight
facts: Samarra served as an Abbasid capital from 836 to 892.
It was the second Abbasid capital after Baghdad.
Its surviving plan helps researchers study an early Islamic capital.
The archaeological city preserves mosque and palace remains.
The Al-Malwiya and Abu Dulaf mosques form part of the site.
Carved stucco associated with Samarra influenced decoration elsewhere.
Early abandonment helped preserve the ancient city plan.
The remains are evidence of Abbasid architecture rather than a complete surviving city.
